quizzes.title: COP17 Finance and Partnerships
quizzes.passage:
The United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification is one of three Rio Conventions, along with the UNFCCC and the CBD. It was adopted on 17 June 1994, a date now observed as World Day to Combat Desertification. It is the principal international legally binding framework dealing with desertification, land degradation and drought, and its core objective is to promote sustainable land management. The convention aims to achieve land degradation neutrality by 2030, a goal linked with SDG Target 15.3.

The seventeenth Conference of the Parties concluded in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, under the theme 'Restoring Land. Restoring Hope.' The meeting coincided with the UN International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists 2026, which placed greater emphasis on pastoral communities and sustainable rangeland management.

Land degradation has emerged as a major threat to ecosystems, agriculture and economic stability. The convention has built platforms that bring together public money and private investors. One of these is a drought partnership that was launched at an earlier COP and aims to help countries that are vulnerable to drought. Another is a major platform through which the convention involves the private sector in land-related work.

COP17 also promoted several approaches that rely on healthy ecosystems. Mongolia highlighted the severity of its own land degradation challenge during the meeting.

questions.q: Which platform is described in the booklet as UNCCD's major means of involving the private sector in sustainable land management, water management and land restoration?
questions.explanation: The booklet names the Business4Land Initiative as UNCCD's major platform for involving the private sector.

questions.q: According to the booklet, COP17 promoted ecosystem restoration within which kind of planning?
questions.explanation: The booklet says COP17 promoted Ecosystem Restoration in National Development Planning.

questions.q:
Read the assertion and reason below and choose the correct option.
Assertion (A): The Riyadh Global Drought Resilience Partnership initially secured around USD 2.15 billion in commitments.
Reason (R): The partnership aims to support 80 vulnerable and drought-affected countries through public and private finance.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements appear in the booklet, but the aim of supporting 80 countries does not explain the commitments secured.

questions.q: What approach does the booklet say the land degradation crisis highlights the need for?
options: Landscape-level restoration rather than isolated interventions
questions.explanation: The booklet says the crisis highlights the need for landscape-level restoration rather than isolated interventions.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Riyadh Global Drought Resilience Partnership was launched during UNCCD COP 16 in Riyadh in 2024.
II. Business4Land Initiative covers sustainable land management, water management and land restoration.
III. The Riyadh Global Drought Resilience Partnership was launched during COP17 in Ulaanbaatar.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while III wrongly places the partnership's launch at COP17.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are true?
Business4Land Initiative covers water management as well as land restoration.
The Riyadh partnership aims to support 100 vulnerable countries.
COP17 promoted greater adoption of Nature-based Solutions.
questions.explanation: The first and third statements match the booklet, while the target of 100 countries contradicts the booklet's figure of 80.

questions.q: According to the booklet, what is the stated objective of using healthy ecosystems?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the objective is to use healthy ecosystems as a means of strengthening climate and drought resilience.

quizzes.title: India's Land Restoration Programmes
quizzes.passage:
The United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification is one of three Rio Conventions, along with the UNFCCC and the CBD. It is the principal international legally binding framework dealing with desertification, land degradation and drought. Its core objective is to promote sustainable land management, and it is linked with SDG Target 15.3.

Land degradation neutrality describes a condition in which the quantity and quality of land resources needed to support ecosystem functions and services remain stable or improve.

The most recent conference of the Parties was held in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, under the theme 'Restoring Land. Restoring Hope.' It coincided with the UN International Year of Rangelands and Pastoralists 2026, which placed greater emphasis on pastoral communities and sustainable rangeland management.

Land degradation has emerged as a major threat to ecosystems, agriculture and economic stability. Mongolia highlighted the severity of its own land degradation challenge during the meeting. The booklet describes an objective of using healthy ecosystems as a means of strengthening climate and drought resilience.

India attended the meeting and presented its own work on land. India also runs several national programmes that address land degradation, which the booklet describes as part of its own land efforts. The meeting also promoted greater use of nature-based approaches, which relate to ecosystems and development planning.

questions.q: In which year was the National Action Plan to Combat Desertification introduced?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the plan was introduced in 2001 and revised in 2023.

questions.q: Which of the following ecosystems is named as covered by India's Guide to Grasslands and Other Open Natural Ecosystems?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the Thar Desert among the ecosystems the guide seeks to recognise and conserve.

questions.q:
Read the assertion and reason below and choose the correct option.
Assertion (A): India has brought around 21.76 million hectares of degraded and deforested land under restoration under the Bonn Challenge.
Reason (R): This is part of India's broader target of restoring 26 million hectares by 2030.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements appear in the booklet, but a broader target does not explain the area already brought under restoration.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Green India Mission   ->   A. Overarching framework for coordinating interventions on land restoration and desertification control
II. Mission Amrit Sarovar   ->   B. Creation and rejuvenation of water bodies
III. Aravalli Green Wall Initiative   ->   C. Restoration of degraded areas associated with the Aravalli landscape
IV. National Action Plan to Combat Desertification   ->   D. Forest restoration and enhancement of carbon sequestration
questions.explanation: The booklet links Green India Mission with forest restoration, Amrit Sarovar with water bodies, the Aravalli initiative with degraded Aravalli areas, and the action plan with the overarching framework.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. India is a Party to the UNCCD.
II. India's Guide to Grasslands and Other Open Natural Ecosystems was launched at COP 16 in Riyadh.
III. The Guide covers the Deccan Savannas and Ravines among other open ecosystems.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while II wrongly gives COP 16 in Riyadh as the launch venue, which was COP17.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are true?
The National Action Plan to Combat Desertification was revised in 2023.
The Aravalli Green Wall Initiative focuses on the creation of water bodies.
The Green India Mission is a component of the National Action Plan on Climate Change.
questions.explanation: The first and third statements match the booklet, while the water bodies work belongs to Mission Amrit Sarovar, not the Aravalli initiative.

questions.q: What did India launch at COP17 to improve recognition of ecosystems such as the Thar Desert and Banni Grasslands?
options: Guide to Grasslands and Other Open Natural Ecosystems
questions.explanation: The booklet says India launched the Guide to Grasslands and Other Open Natural Ecosystems at COP17.
